key_insight: The paper shows that current AI theorem-proving agents can solve nontrivial Lean 4 proofs in quantum algorithms and quantum information, and that adding a verified domain library consistently improves performance.
engineering_relevance: The benchmarks provide a reproducible way to measure and compare proof-agent reliability for quantum software verification and formal methods workflows.
method: Built two Lean 4 benchmarks: Lean-QuantumAlg-Bench (36 tasks) and Lean-QIT-Bench (40 tasks).
Evaluated GPT-5.5, Kimi K3, DeepSeek V4-Pro, and MiniMax M3 in a common theorem-proving framework.
Compared a task-only baseline against library-augmented deduction (LAD) with access to a verified domain library.
evidence_signal: All tasks compile in a fixed environment and are scored with deterministic proof checking plus targeted semantic review; the best difficulty-weighted scores were 60.4/100 and 59.6/100, and LAD improved score and completion rate in all 8 model-benchmark comparisons.
watch_item: Results depend on a fixed Lean environment and benchmark-specific task set, so gains may not transfer directly to broader quantum formalization workloads.
paper_title: Benchmarking Agents for Proving Theorems in Quantum Algorithms and Quantum Information
